title: Guest access: who can your tenant invite, and what can guests reach?
summary: The guest-access mechanism, licensing statements and control calls are supported by Microsoft documentation. The invitation path stops early in the documented procedure, and the checklist names cross-tenant device trust without a corresponding control row; these are minor corrections.

claims.claim: Guest access uses Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration, part of Microsoft Entra External ID, to share tenant resources with external people.
claims.quote: Microsoft Entra External ID includes collaboration capabilities that allow your workforce to work securely with business partners and guests.

claims.claim: Invited partners sign in with their own identities and credentials.
claims.quote: A simple invitation and redemption process lets partners use their own credentials to access your company's resources.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Partners do not need a Microsoft Entra account to collaborate.
claims.quote: The partner uses their own identities and credentials, whether or not they have a Microsoft Entra account.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Guests who redeem an invitation or complete self-service sign-up are represented by user objects in the resource directory.
claims.quote: Once the guest redeems their invitation or completes sign-up, they're represented in your directory as a user object.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: B2B collaboration users typically have user type Guest.
claims.quote: The user type for these B2B collaboration users is typically set to "guest"

claims.where: What it is: How it works

claims.quote: their user principal name contains the #EXT# identifier.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: B2B collaboration is enabled by default.
claims.quote: B2B collaboration is enabled by default

claims.quote: External collaboration settings let you specify what roles in your organization can invite external users for B2B collaboration.

claims.claim: External collaboration settings govern which domains can receive invitations.
claims.quote: You can use collaboration restrictions to allow or deny invitations to the domains you specify.

claims.claim: External collaboration settings govern how much of the directory guests can see.

claims.claim: Cross-tenant access settings govern authentication with other Microsoft Entra tenants.
claims.quote: Cross-tenant access settings control whether users can authenticate with external Microsoft Entra tenants.

claims.claim: Cross-tenant access settings govern both inbound and outbound B2B collaboration.
claims.quote: They apply to both inbound and outbound B2B collaboration.

claims.claim: Cross-tenant access can be scoped to users, groups and applications.
claims.quote: Manage inbound and outbound B2B collaboration, and scope access to specific users, groups, and applications.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: The most restrictive external collaboration or cross-tenant setting applies where both govern an invitation.
claims.quote: In this case, the most restrictive setting applies. Your external collaboration settings prevent your users from sending invitations to users at adatum.com.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: A blocked domain prevents new invitations even if cross-tenant access permits that organisation.
claims.quote: You allow B2B collaboration with Fabrikam in your cross-tenant access settings, but then you add fabrikam.com to your blocked domains in your external collaboration settings. Your users can't invite new Fabrikam business guests

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Existing guests can continue working when their domain is subsequently blocked for invitations.
claims.quote: existing Fabrikam guests can continue using B2B collaboration.

claims.quote: Guests are added to your organization's Microsoft Entra ID as B2B collaboration users.

claims.quote: External access - A feature that allows users to find, call, and chat with people who have Microsoft identities, including those from other organizations.

claims.claim: Teams external access does not give team membership.
claims.quote: External user access includes invitations, calls, chats, and meetings, but doesn't include team membership and access to the resources of the team.

claims.where: What it is: Where guests are used
claims.claim: Teams external access does not give access to team resources.
claims.quote: | Access Teams resources | No | Yes |

claims.claim: SharePoint and OneDrive can use B2B authentication when their integration is enabled.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Open invitations
claims.claim: Outside US Government, allowInvitesFrom defaults to everyone, allowing members and guests to invite more guests.
claims.quote: Allow everyone in the organization, including guests, to invite guests. The default setting for all cloud environments except US Government.

claims.claim: Invitations can be sent to any domain by default.
claims.quote: By default, the Allow invitations to be sent to any domain (most inclusive) setting is enabled.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Open invitations
claims.claim: US Government defaults allowInvitesFrom to none.
claims.quote: none | Prevent everyone, including admins, from inviting guests. Default setting for US Government.

claims.claim: The none invitation setting prevents everyone, including administrators, from inviting guests.
claims.quote: Prevent everyone, including admins, from inviting guests.

claims.claim: External ID billing uses MAU, the unique external users who authenticate to the tenants within a calendar month.
claims.quote: The basic External ID billing model is based on monthly active users (MAU), which is the count of unique external users who authenticate to your tenants within a calendar month.

claims.claim: The External ID MAU billing model applies to all guest users.
claims.quote: The MAU billing model for External ID applies to all guest users.

claims.claim: For B2B collaboration, MAU billing applies to external users with UserType Guest, not Member.
claims.quote: For B2B collaboration, the MAU billing model applies only to external users who have a UserType value of Guest.

claims.claim: Microsoft's External ID FAQ states that the core offering is free for the first 50,000 MAU.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Entra External ID core offering is free for the first 50,000 MAU.

claims.claim: External ID requires an Azure subscription for billing.
claims.quote: External ID requires an Azure subscription for billing.

claims.claim: The workforce tenant must be linked to an Azure subscription.
claims.quote: Microsoft Entra workforce tenants must be linked to an Azure subscription for proper billing and access to features.

claims.claim: Premium add-on charges are additional to basic MAU billing.
claims.quote: Premium add-on charges are in addition to the basic MAU billing.

claims.claim: ID Governance is a MAU-based add-on for guest users in workforce tenants.
claims.quote: | ID Governance | Workforce | MAU-based | Govern guest users with premium features in Microsoft Entra ID Governance.

claims.claim: GSA for Guests is a MAU-based add-on for guests in workforce tenants.
claims.quote: | GSA for Guests | Workforce | MAU-based | Global Secure Access (GSA) coverage for guest users in workforce tenants. |

claims.claim: Learn directs readers to aka.ms/ExternalIDPricing for current basic and add-on prices.
claims.quote:
For the latest pricing details, see External ID pricing.
For the latest information about add-on pricing, see External ID pricing.

claims.claim: Conditional Access requires access to Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2.
claims.quote: Access to Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 edition, which includes Conditional Access policy capabilities.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Lists are not retroactive
claims.claim: The domain invitation list does not apply to guests who already redeemed invitations and does not revoke their access.
claims.quote: The list doesn't apply to external users who already redeemed the invitation.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Lists are not retroactive
claims.claim: A pending invitation fails at redemption if the invited user's domain is subsequently blocked.
claims.quote: If a user invitation is in a pending state, and you set a policy that blocks their domain, the user's attempt to redeem the invitation fails.

claims.claim: The Entra domain invitation list is independent of the SharePoint and OneDrive sharing lists.
claims.quote: This list works independently from OneDrive and SharePoint Online allow/block lists. If you want to restrict individual file sharing in SharePoint Online, you need to set up an allow or block list for OneDrive and SharePoint Online.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Domain lists; controls[2].note
claims.claim: An organisation can configure either an allow list or a block list, not both.
claims.quote: You can create either an allow list or a block list. You can't set up both types of lists.

claims.claim: Switching between allow and block lists discards the existing configuration.
claims.quote: Switching from one policy to another discards the existing policy configuration.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Microsoft's pages differ
claims.claim: The architecture guide says inbound cross-tenant access controls application access and token issuance, not invitation or redemption.
claims.quote: Cross-tenant access settings, inbound access does not prevent users from sending invitations, nor prevent them from being redeemed. However, it does control application access and whether a token is issued to the Guest User.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Microsoft's pages differ; Governance controls: Interaction
claims.claim: The configuration guide says domain lists and cross-tenant access settings are checked at invitation.
claims.quote: Both allow/block list and cross-tenant access settings are checked at the time of invitation.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Microsoft's pages differ
claims.claim: The configuration guide says inbound B2B Block access can prevent invitations.
claims.quote: Block access: Blocks the users and groups specified under Applies to from being invited to B2B collaboration.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Microsoft's pages differ
claims.claim: Cross-tenant access settings apply to Microsoft Entra tenants.
claims.quote: Cross-tenant access settings apply to Microsoft Entra tenants.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Microsoft's pages differ
claims.claim: External collaboration settings control partners who do not use Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: To control access for partners not using Microsoft Entra ID, use external collaboration settings.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Microsoft's pages differ
claims.claim: Changing cross-tenant defaults to Block access can cut existing business-critical access.
claims.quote: Changing the default inbound or outbound settings to Block access could block existing business-critical access to apps in your organization or partner organizations.

claims.claim: Only one organisation can manage a device.
claims.quote: Only one organization can manage a device.

claims.claim: Device-compliance policies can block guests.
claims.quote: If device compliance is required but can't be evaluated, access is blocked for both B2B collaboration and B2B direct connect users.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Device policies; What to check
claims.claim: Inbound cross-tenant device trust can accept home-tenant compliance claims instead of excluding guests from device-compliance requirements.
claims.quote: Grant controls - Require compliant device | Supported, requires configuring your inbound trust settings to accept compliant device claims from the external organization.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Targeting all users
claims.claim: Conditional Access All users includes B2B guests.
claims.quote: All users in the directory, including B2B guests.

claims.quote: If you turn guest access off in Teams, existing guests lose access to their team.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Turning Teams guest access off

claims.quote: However, they are not removed from the team.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Turning Teams guest access off

claims.claim: Guest invitation settings are at Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > External Identities > External collaboration settings > Guest invite settings.
claims.quote:
Browse to Entra ID > External Identities > External collaboration settings.
Under Guest invite settings, choose the appropriate settings:

claims.claim: PATCH /v1.0/policies/authorizationPolicy sets invitation permissions through allowInvitesFrom with the four listed values.
claims.quote: allowInvitesFrom | allowInvitesFrom | Indicates who can invite external users to the organization. The possible values are: none, adminsAndGuestInviters, adminsGuestInvitersAndAllMembers, everyone.

claims.claim: Guest Inviter lets named users invite guests when only specific administrator roles may invite.
claims.quote: Users with the Guest Inviter role are able to invite guests even when the option Only users assigned to specific admin roles can invite guest users is selected (under Guest invite settings).

claims.claim: Directory visibility settings are at Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > External Identities > External collaboration settings > Guest user access.
claims.quote:
Browse to Entra ID > External Identities > External collaboration settings.
Under Guest user access, choose the level of access you want guest users to have:

claims.claim: PATCH /v1.0/policies/authorizationPolicy configures guest directory access through guestUserRoleId.
claims.quote:
PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/policies/authorizationPolicy

guestUserRoleId | Guid | Represents role templateId for the role that should be granted to guest user.

claims.claim: guestUserRoleId supports the User, Guest User and Restricted Guest User roles.
claims.quote: Currently following roles are supported: User (a0b1b346-4d3e-4e8b-98f8-753987be4970), Guest User (10dae51f-b6af-4016-8d66-8c2a99b929b3), and Restricted Guest User (2af84b1e-32c8-42b7-82bc-daa82404023b).

claims.claim: The domain block list is at Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > External Identities > External collaboration settings > Collaboration restrictions > Deny invitations to the specified domains > Target domains.
claims.quote:
Browse to Entra ID > External Identities > External collaboration settings.
Under Collaboration restrictions, select Deny invitations to the specified domains.
Under Target domains, enter the name of one of the domains that you want to block.

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/policies/b2bManagementPolicies/{b2bManagementPolicyId} updates the domain policy through definition.
claims.quote:
PATCH /policies/b2bManagementPolicies/{b2bManagementPolicyId}

definition | String collection | A string collection containing a JSON string that defines the rules and settings for a policy.

claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version in Microsoft Graph are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: The alternative allow-list option is Allow invitations only to the specified domains.
claims.quote: Under Collaboration restrictions, select Allow invitations only to the specified domains (most restrictive).

claims.claim: Inbound B2B defaults are reached through the listed Cross-tenant access settings, Default settings, Edit inbound defaults, B2B collaboration, External users and groups and Access status route.
claims.quote:
Browse to Entra ID > External Identities > Cross-tenant access settings, then select Cross-tenant access settings.
Default settings: To modify default inbound settings, select the Default settings tab, and then under Inbound access settings, select Edit inbound defaults.

claims.claim: PATCH /v1.0/policies/crossTenantAccessPolicy/default configures defaults through b2bCollaborationInbound and b2bCollaborationOutbound.
claims.quote:
PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/policies/crossTenantAccessPolicy/default

claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least a Security Administrator.

claims.claim: Organisation-specific cross-tenant access settings are under Organizational settings.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > External Identities > Cross-tenant access settings, then select Organizational settings.

claims.claim: An individual guest invitation starts at Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > Users > New user > Invite external user.
claims.quote:
Browse to Entra ID > Users.
Select New user and then Invite external user.
Under Identity on the Basics tab, enter the email address of the external user.
Select Review + invite to automatically send the invitation to the guest user.
claims.fix: Extend controls[4].ui.path and its rendered table path to 'Entra ID > Users > New user > Invite external user > Basics > Identity > Review + invite'. The existing steps are correct but stop on the invitation form before the invitation action.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/invitations invites an external user identified by invitedUserEmailAddress.
claims.quote:
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/invitations

invitedUserEmailAddress | string | The email address of the user you're inviting.

claims.claim: The invitation API can also reset redemption status for a guest who already redeemed an invitation.
claims.quote: Use this API to create a new invitation or reset the redemption status for a guest user who already redeemed their invitation.

claims.claim: The listed Conditional Access policy creation route reaches Include > Select users and groups > Guest or external users.
claims.quote:
Browse to Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies.
Select New policy.
Under Assignments, select Users or workload identities.
Under Include, choose Select users and groups, and then select Guest or external users.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/identity/conditionalAccess/policies creates a Conditional Access policy.
claims.quote:
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/identity/conditionalAccess/policies

In the request body, supply a JSON representation of a conditionalAccessPolicy object.

claims.claim: The portal procedure to create Conditional Access policies requires at least Conditional Access Administrator.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least a Conditional Access Administrator.

claims.claim: Teams guest access is configured at Teams admin center > Users > Guest access > Guest access.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Teams admin center.
Select Users > Guest access.
Set Guest access to On.

claims.claim: The MicrosoftTeams cmdlet Set-CsTeamsClientConfiguration -AllowGuestUser $true allows guests to access the Teams client.
claims.quote: Designates whether or not guest users in your organization will have access to the Teams client. If $true, guests in your tenant will be able to access the Teams client.

claims.claim: Guest Screen sharing is configurable on the same Teams Guest access page.
claims.quote: Screen sharing– This setting controls the availability of screen sharing for guests.

claims.claim: Guest Meet now in channels is configurable on the same Teams Guest access page.
claims.quote: Meet now in channels – Turn this setting On to allow guests to use the Meet Now feature in Microsoft Teams.

claims.claim: External collaboration portal settings require a role such as Global Administrator or External Identity Provider Administrator that can update them.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Entra admin center, you need a role that can update external collaboration settings, such as Global Administrator or External Identity Provider Administrator.

claims.claim: The domain allow or block list portal procedure specifies Global Administrator.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as a Global Administrator.

claims.claim: The guest invitation portal tutorial specifies at least User Administrator.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least a User Administrator.

claims.claim: Teams guest access also depends on separate settings in Entra ID, Microsoft 365 Groups and SharePoint.
claims.quote: Guest access in Teams also requires configuring other settings in Microsoft 365, including settings in Microsoft Entra ID, Microsoft 365 Groups, and SharePoint.
